item.title: Online Seakeeping Forecast Coupling System Identification With Nonlinear Pseudo Spectral Potential-Flow
item.description: arXiv:2610.28694v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a grey-box framework for a robust deterministic, real-time prediction of coupled surge-heave-pitch motion in waves. The approach combines a physics-based online system identification with a nonlinear pseudo-spectral potential flow solver. Rather than prescribing a complete hydrodynamic model from captive model tests or relying on a black-box surrogate, three coupled compact, dynamics equations are identified with constrained ridge-regression of a short time-history of free-running body motion data in waves. The PSPF solver is then used to provide the future incident wave at the body's location. The PSPF and dynamic system models are coupled for continuous real-time future motion prediction in a receding horizon architecture, while the model coefficients are re-identified online to enable robust prediction to changing wave-conditions. This novel framework is demonstrated based on CFD data that has been validated for a freely floating two-dimensional rectangular box in waves. The results demonstrate a feasible framework for accurate motion forecasting up to around eight wavelengths into the future utilising data that can be gathered onboard a ship in real operations. Furthermore, it is shown that the framework is robust to changing sea-states and agnostic to underlying model geometry.
item.dc:creator: Zev Hoffman, Sara Vahaji, Micheal Candon, Nirman Jayarathne, Pier Marzocca

item.title: Monocular 3D bubble reconstruction: DNS-informed ray tracing and deep learning
item.description: arXiv:2610.28908v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bubble size, depth, and spatial distribution govern transport and uniformity in multiphase flows. A single shadowgraphic view cannot separate bubble diameter from focal-plane displacement, as image signatures depend on both, while multicamera systems add optical access, calibration, and cost. We develop a single-camera physics-guided framework combining direct numerical simulation (DNS), validated Monte Carlo ray tracing, preprocessing, and focus-conditioned multitask deep learning to recover three-dimensional bubble position and physical-equivalent diameter from two-dimensional shadowgraphs. DNS-resolved bubble label images rendered at multiple focal-plane settings. The ray tracer reproduces shadowgraphic signatures with errors below $3\%$ (intensity), $1\%$ (apparent size), $15\%$ (blur), $6\%$ (numerical aperture), and $4\%$ (edge-spread-function shape), running $\sim30\times$ faster than the CPU implementation. The dataset has $900$ frames and $87{,}728$ labeled instances, partitioned by DNS timestamp to prevent leakage and expanded to over $10^{5}$ crops by broad-depth controlled-density rendering. A multitask network predicts signed depth and diameter from crops and focal-plane coordinates, achieving $\sim97.6\%$ normalized depth accuracy on held-out data; a closed-loop DNS-to-image-to-reconstruction test of $180$ bubbles gives diameter error below $9.71\%$ ($\sim90.29\%$ accuracy). On experimental images at four radial planes ($142$--$971$ bubbles each), PDF overlap is $68\%$--$92\%$ and log-PDF correlation is $0.72$--$0.87$. At the focal reference plane ($11{,}679$ bubbles), overlap is $\sim86\%$, correlation is $0.93$, and full-distribution, $D_{99.8}$, and composite errors are below $7.7\%$, increasing with focal-plane distance and defining a recoverability limit. Without stereoscopic hardware, the framework offers a scalable diagnostic for dense bubbly flows.
item.dc:creator: Chaitanya S. Nayak, Faizaan Mohammed, Vivek Kumar, Shivam Prajapati, Suhas S. Jain, Cyrus K. Aidun

item.title: Computational and experimental study of multi-grain-size sediment transport and sorting process
item.description: arXiv:2610.29072v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Successful prediction of the interaction between turbulent flows and river ecosystems is essential for flood management, development of mitigation strategies, and infrastructure protection. Natural riverbeds consist of bed materials of multiple grain sizes that interact with turbulence differently, leading to spatial classification of particle sizes. Such particle sorting processes can only be captured by models capable of handling multiple grain sizes. We present a numerical framework that couples large-eddy simulation with a multi-grain-size sediment transport module to track multiple grain size classes, their local fractions within the bed-load layer, and bed evolution. A laboratory experiment was conducted in a flume with multi-size bed material to examine sediment particle redistribution and sorting. Measured sediment grain size distributions and bed elevations were used to validate the numerical framework. The results of the multi-grain-size sediment transport model for bed deformation were then compared against those of a uniform sediment transport model, demonstrating that the former reduces the prediction errors relative to the experimental measurements from 37.98 to 3.83 percent for maximum scour depth and from 48.35 to 11.54 percent for maximum deposition height. The validated numerical framework was also applied to large-scale meandering rivers with multi-grain bed material, simulating their bed deformation and sediment sorting. The simulation results revealed the formation of particle sorting patterns in meandering rivers, with coarser and finer sediment particles accumulating near the erosional depression (scour) and depositional (point bar) regions, respectively. These findings support the coupled framework's ability to predict sediment particle sorting and highlight the importance of representing bed material heterogeneity in numerical modeling of meandering rivers.
item.dc:creator: Mehrshad Gholami Anjiraki, Gabriel Narh, Jonathan Craig, Mustafa Meri\c{c} Aksen, Samin Shapourmiandouab, Ali Farhadzadeh, Tao Xiang, Ali Khosronejad

item.title: Dynamics of liquid jet breakup and droplet size distribution in a crossflow airstream
item.description: arXiv:2610.29193v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The fragmentation of a liquid jet in a crossflowing airstream arises from a complex interplay between aerodynamic forcing and interfacial instabilities acting across a wide range of length scales. We examine the spatial evolution of droplet size distributions along the jet trajectory using a combination of high-speed shadowgraphy and digital in-line holography, allowing simultaneous characterization of jet morphology and volumetric droplet size distributions. The results demonstrate a clear progression of breakup mechanisms, from near-field bag rupture to downstream rim, ligament, and node disintegration, each associated with distinct characteristic length scales. This evolution is reflected in the droplet size distributions, which broaden and become increasingly polydisperse downstream relative to the near-field distributions. By systematically varying the liquid-jet and airstream Weber numbers, we identify distinct breakup modes, and construct a regime map that delineates the column-breakup, isolated-bag-breakup, and interacting-bag regimes. Furthermore, by incorporating the dominant instability mechanisms, including Rayleigh-Taylor and Rayleigh-Plateau instabilities associated with the observed column, bag, and multi-bag breakup modes, we develop a theoretical framework for jet atomization in crossflow. The framework relates instability wavelengths to characteristic droplet sizes, and reasonably captures the experimentally observed trends. We found that stronger aerodynamic forcing induces earlier breakup, decreases the characteristic instability length scales, and generates finer droplets dispersed over a wider spatial region. Overall, the study establishes a quantitative relationship between instability-driven fragmentation dynamics and droplet size distributions, thereby connecting interfacial instabilities with measurable spray characteristics.
item.dc:creator: Gowri Padmaja Majji, Aman John Tudu, Lakshmana Dora Chandrala, Kirti Chandra Sahu

item.title: Automated Discovery of Physically Interpretable Subgrid Length Scales for Detached Eddy Simulation via Agentic AI
item.description: arXiv:2610.29850v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Traditional turbulence-model development relies heavily on expert knowledge and is time-consuming. This study develops an agentic AI framework, DEScover (automated Discovery of DES closures), to explore subgrid length scales for detached eddy simulation (DES). The user provides only a modeling idea: the length scale is the grid width normal to the local vortex axis. Four large language model (LLM) agents then propose, review, implement, and evaluate candidate formulations and generate scripts for CFD simulations. The Discovery Agent infers the vortex axis from various vortex-identification methods. The candidates are tested on four cases spanning canonical and engineering flows: a flat plate, a backward-facing step, a free shear layer, and an iced airfoil. For all test cases, the best candidate consistently outperforms the standard length scale based on the maximum cell size. Its accuracy is similar to, or slightly better than, that of the expert-designed shear-layer-adapted length scale. Each agentic discovery run takes about 25 minutes on average, excluding the CFD simulations. These results show that LLM-based reasoning can significantly accelerate the discovery of physically interpretable turbulence models and reduce reliance on manual expert formulation.
item.dc:creator: Jiawei Chen, Xiang I. A. Yang, Ping He

item.title: Acoustic control of Rayleigh-regime liquid-jet breakup using a through-hole MHz transducer
item.description: arXiv:2610.29899v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This experimental study demonstrates MHz-order acoustic control of Rayleigh-regime liquid-jet breakup using a compact through-hole lithium niobate thickness-mode transducer integrated at the nozzle exit and driven near its 6.7 MHz resonance. Jet dynamics were measured by high-speed shadowgraphy at 50,000 fps, and breakup lengths were obtained from instantaneous jet-length records using an autocorrelation-based method that identifies statistically separated breakup events. Acoustic actuation produced visible interfacial corrugations and reduced the normalized breakup length, $L_b/d$, for both water and glycerol--water jets. In water, the response was threshold-like at low Weber number and weakened as the jet velocity increased to We ~ 50. A reduced-order threshold correlation, fit to the water amplitude and velocity sweeps, captured this abrupt shortening and the subsequent loss of actuation efficacy. More viscous glycerol--water mixtures shortened immediately at low forcing, indicating a distinct acoustic-coupling regime rather than a universal collapse of the water response. A wetting-control experiment showed that liquid spreading at the nozzle base can also shorten the jet, so the measured response reflects coupled radiation-pressure forcing, capillary-wave feedback, and wetting-mediated disturbance injection. Resolved droplet tracking further showed that MHz excitation changes the visible gate-crossing droplet population, although sub-resolution mist and micron-scale atomization were not measured. These results establish through-hole MHz actuation as a compact route for modifying free-surface jet breakup and provide a repeatable image-analysis protocol for experimental-fluid-mechanics measurements.
item.dc:creator: Kha Nguyen, Kareem Ahmed, James Friend

item.title: Hydrodynamics of microalgae in sea spray
item.description: arXiv:2610.29719v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Airborne transmission of biological matter is likely to cause numerous respiratory distress in coastal populations during certain harmful algal blooms. While we know that dissolved algal toxins aerosolize, the contribution of particle-associated toxins is still unknown. The observation of microalgae in the atmosphere suggests that cells or cell debris could be a carrier. Exchange of particulate matter between ocean and atmosphere is driven by sea spray: microplastics and bacteria aerosolize in jet droplets, following the bursting of air bubbles. However, current models for particle capture only consider surface effects, which fail to explain how large microalgal cells (5-50 um) can be entrapped in jet drops (100-800 um). Here, we demonstrate with a variety of species that microalgae are consistently captured in jet drops, and derive a new particle capture model based on the hydrodynamics of the jet. Using the enrichment factor, which measures the increase in concentration in the first jet drop relative to the bulk, we uncover two regimes. The transition between regimes strongly depends on cell size. In addition, we highlight the dynamics of particles within the jet and derive an enrichment model based on hydrodynamics rather than surface considerations. This work widens and generalizes established results on bacterial and microplastic entrapment in jet drops, resolving discrepancies found in the literature. Finally, we demonstrate that sea spray can aerosolize toxic Ostreopsis cf. ovata cells. This reveals a potential particulate pathway for airborne toxicity during harmful algal blooms and raises the question of the relative contribution of particles to that of dissolved toxins.
item.dc:creator: Elettra Fig\`a Talamanca, Juliette Pierre, Eva Ternon, Paula Cohen, Maarten De Rijcke, H\'el\`ene de Maleprade

item.title: Swarmlet: a GPU-resident reformulated vortex particle method for coupled multirotor aerodynamics and flight dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.29867v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present Swarmlet, a GPU solver for the unsteady aerodynamics and flight dynamics of one or many multirotor vehicles. The wake is a meshless, evolving-core vortex particle field in the reformulated (rVPM) large-eddy formulation, coupled to rotor models of three fidelities, six-degree-of-freedom vehicles and flight control. Particles carry a smooth core of compact support whose field outside four core radii is exactly the singular Biot-Savart field, so the multipole far field of the treecode carries no regularization error. The subfilter closure is a dynamic eddy viscosity on a fixed filter width, applied by core spreading with a Lagrangian exchange of its local excess under an explicit stability bound, and the strengths are relaxed by projection; global corrections make both the exchange and the relaxation conserve total vorticity and linear impulse. All rotor models shed connected bound circulation, the disks along the arcs swept in each step however long, so the wake receives the lift impulse. The solver agrees with direct summation to $5\times 10^{-7}$ and converges at third order in time. Without calibration, an actuator-line model that includes its own near sheet predicts the hover thrust of a DJI 9443 propeller within 2%. With calibrated section polars it reproduces a Crazyflie propeller's thrust and torque within 3.2% at three speeds and the near wake of a hovering quadrotor with relative $L^2$ differences of 0.08-0.21 against particle image velocimetry, while the wake keeps the delivered impulse. A closed-loop formation of 100 quadrotors, run at a coarser setting on one GPU, illustrates the coupled method at swarm scale.
item.dc:creator: Wyatt James Horne

item.title: DiffVortex: A quantum-inspired fast solver for incompressible flows
item.description: arXiv:2610.30012v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Matrix-product-state (MPS) and quantized tensor-train (QTT) representations offer a promising framework for computational fluid dynamics, with logarithmic run time and memory scaling in mesh size when bond dimensions remain bounded. Existing MPS-based solvers are Eulerian: they compress velocity fields and enforce immersed-body boundary conditions through static masks or body-fitted coordinates. Moving or flexible bodies complicate this approach: deformation requires updating MPS masks every time step, while filamentary vorticity in high-Reynolds-number flows may resist low-rank compression. We propose a complementary approach: compress the Biot--Savart kernel rather than the flow state, evolve vorticity using Lagrangian vortex particles, and represent immersed bodies by bound vortex sheets on Lagrangian surface points. Our main theoretical result is a lifting theorem: QTT rank $r$ of the kernel implies matrix-product-operator (MPO) rank at most $2^d r$ for the corresponding convolution operator in $d$ dimensions, independent of grid resolution. This bound is sharp for our interleaved ordering. With quantics tensor cross interpolation, the moment-to-local stage of a single-level fast multipole method becomes a precomputed tensor-network contraction with quasi-linear complexity, retaining Lagrangian flexibility for immersed bodies. Our PyTorch implementation (\texttt{DiffVortex}) is end-to-end differentiable, runs on GPUs, and handles $6.7\times10^{7}$ particles on a single device. We validate against reference vortex-method results for an impulsively started cylinder and exact and reference solutions for inviscid elliptical vortices. We also demonstrate two-dimensional flows past rigidly moving, multiple, and deforming bodies, including gradients propagated through the full time integration.
item.dc:creator: Yu Jun Loo, Silas Alben, Shravan Veerapaneni

item.title: Data-Free Finite-Volume Convolutional Neural Networks for Steady Compressible Euler Flow around a Circular Cylinder
item.description: arXiv:2603.01001v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A data-free finite-volume convolutional neural network (FV-CNN) is formulated for steady Euler flow around a cylinder at eight Mach numbers, 2--15. Shared-face fluxes define conservative spatial balances, while automatic differentiation supplies parameter gradients. The derivative mismatch in the earlier automatic-differentiation-based convolutional neural network (AD-CNN) is derived. No computational fluid dynamics (CFD) or experimental field targets enter training; reference-independent selection of coefficients, seeds, and checkpoints is not established. Billig-based upstream fixing conditions shock-location agreement.For eight adopted fields, density and pressure relative $L_2$ discrepancies from finite-resolution CFD are $5.43$--$18.69\%$ and $6.25$--$19.70\%$. Closed-band defects are smaller than AD-CNN in 32/32 self-centered and 22--31/32 CFD-centered comparisons over seven half-widths, 0.06--0.12 cylinder diameters. AD-CNN retains smaller enthalpy root-mean-square (RMS) discrepancies in 7/8 cases, shock-position RMS at Mach 11 and 15, and temperature and transverse-velocity discrepancies at Mach 3.Ten new Mach-15 initializations and adopted seed 42 yield density discrepancies of $12.04$--$43.70\%$ (mean $24.34\%$, sample standard deviation $11.78$ percentage points); the new ten alone give $25.04\%$ and $12.17$ points. Dispersion exceeds the historical adopted-field gap of $3.40$ points; six of eleven outcomes are below AD-CNN. Transition-width ratios of AD-CNN to FV-CNN remain $4.07$--$4.66$, and all 44 self-centered seed--component balances at half-width 0.10 cylinder diameters are smaller for FV-CNN. Local sharpness and this balance metric persist, while initialization-robust accuracy superiority is not established.Component interventions remain one-seed conditional responses; Mach 2 uses a separate budget-limited protocol.
item.dc:creator: Ryosuke Yano

item.title: Tangential and normal partial slip at the liquid-fluid interfaces: An application to a small liquid droplet, gas bubble, and aerosol
item.description: arXiv:2604.17793v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An analytical solution is obtained for the problem of the slow movement of a small drop of a fluid in another immiscible fluid in an infinitely large reservoir with the boundary condition of the normal slip and(or) tangential partial slip at the liquid-liquid or gas-liquid interface. That generalizes the conventional Navier and Maxwellian boundary conditions of partial slip. Normal slip is accompanied by the density gradient in the fluid and is applicable only if one of the phases in contact at the interface is a gas. At the first time the generalization of the Hadamard-Rybczynski equation (HRE) is discussed within the formalism of two slip lengths. It is proven that each of the two fluids separated by an interface has its own slip length. The slip lengths of the fluids that contact each other through an interface are related by the ratio of the viscosities of these fluids. New equations describing the terminal velocity of gas bubble rise and aerosol falling have been obtained. The theoretical results are in good agreement with the experiments at moderate Knudsen numbers, Kn < 0.25. It has been shown that the gas density within a rising bubble and around a falling droplet in the air is not uniform. The relative magnitude of the density increment increases with the size of the bubble or aerosol. Presumably, the best applicability of the generalized HRE should be expected for the interface of hydrophobic liquid and hydrophilic one (water - hydrocarbons, water - higher alcohols, in general: aqueous emulsions, water - lipophilic organic liquids and oils, etc.). These are quite important emulsions in practical terms, for example, for the oil industry and medicine. Experimental methods for determining the slip length are considered.
item.dc:creator: Peter Lebedev-Stepanov

item.title: Mixing and spreading of gravity currents in heterogeneous porous media
item.description: arXiv:2604.27827v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We analyze the mixing, migration and spreading of a gravity current in a heterogeneous porous medium using high-fidelity numerical simulations. Heterogeneity is represented by log-normal permeability fields of varying correlation lengths and variance. Stable and unstable density stratification scenarios are considered through linear and non-monotonic density laws, respectively. Heterogeneity reduces dissolution and increases the speed of the gravity current proportionally to the Rayleigh number. In the unstable case, heterogeneity accelerates the onset of convection. Convection-driven dissolution slows down the gravity current and counteracts the dispersive effect of heterogeneity resulting in a narrower interface and higher dissolution than in the stable case. Permeability anisotropy reduces dissolution because of the barrier effect of low permeability regions, except when blobs of buoyant fluid are trapped in low permeability structures and rapidly dissolve. The variance of the log-permeability field enhances dissolution. However, the homogeneous case outperforms heterogeneous cases except when Rayleigh number is small. This suggest an interaction between the size of the instabilities, the correlation length of the permeability field and the dispersive and barrier effects of the permeability field that controls dissolution efficiency.
item.dc:creator: Albert Jim\'enez-Ramos, Juan J. Hidalgo

item.title: Bridging the Lattice Boltzmann Method and Moment Methods
item.description: arXiv:2610.26631v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We derive discrete moment equations exactly equivalent to the lattice Boltzmann method (LBM) and identify the general moment closure shared by kinetic methods based on the discrete-velocity Boltzmann equation. This closure provides a route to correct lower-order dynamics without requiring accurate reconstruction of the higher-order moments, thereby substantially broadening the scope of existing closure strategies that seek increasingly accurate representations of these moments. These advances establish a unified moment framework bridging LBM and moment methods. The framework enables efficient simulations across all Knudsen regimes, overcoming the prohibitive complexity of existing moment methods at high Knudsen numbers. It further provides a common basis for integrating and extending key features of diverse kinetic methods.
item.dc:creator: Jinhua Lu, Song Zhao, Pierre Boivin, Pierre Sagaut, Nikolaus A. Adams

item.title: Reduction of Decaying Navier--Stokes Turbulence to the Quantum Pendulum
item.description:
arXiv:2607.05745v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The statistics of a classical flow is a problem of quantum mechanics in loop space, and not by analogy: the loop functional of any flow is the loop-ordered exponential of the covariant derivative $\partial+\mathrm{i}v/
u$. We follow this representation from the Navier--Stokes equation to the Euler ensemble, the fixed point of the loop equation regularized by polygons with $N$ sides. Near the turning angle $ eta=\pi$ an exact operator identity, followed by an asymptotic continuum step and without a saddle-point approximation, reduces the ensemble to two quantum pendulums, the Mathieu equation; this supersedes our earlier WKB evaluation. A Monte Carlo simulation up to $N=10^5$ confirms the reduction. Extreme turbulence has singularities at small scales, and, as in quantum field theory, we define it by this regularization and a renormalization: the leading power of $N$ is removed, and the turbulent viscosity $	ilde
u$ remains as the single physical scale. This is a proposed definition of turbulence at infinite Reynolds number; its continuum spectrum is computed under a stated convergence condition, and its identification with physical turbulence is a hypothesis. The energy spectrum is a function of $\kappa=k\sqrt{	ilde
u(t+t_0)}$ that falls as $1/k$ and then as $k^{-2}$. At $\kappa=\sqrt2$ it has a weak nonanalyticity: its second derivative diverges logarithmically. At a fixed wave number the decay is therefore singular at the finite time $t_*=2/(	ilde
u k^2)-t_0$, when $t_*>0$, and the vorticity correlations oscillate in space with the period $\sqrt2\,\pi\sqrt{	ilde
u(t+t_0)}$. Of the limits of the ensemble with structure, only the pendulum limit is taken at a critical point and has a bulk dissipation that vanishes with the viscosity. A companion paper compares it with simulations and experiments.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Migdal

item.title: The typical red cell makes too little vacuole material for coalescence to build the large vacuoles of pocked cells
item.description: arXiv:2610.22646v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Red blood cells carrying intracellular vacuoles, called pocked cells, are a sensitive marker of splenic function: about 0.5% of cells in healthy people, 20 to 70% after splenectomy. Vacuoles too small to see are common, and visible ones are thought to grow when small ones merge. We tested that idea with a particle model that resolves the cell's membrane, its contents and every vacuole, and with an inventory of the vacuole volume a cell can make. In tube, shear and vascular flows, a cell's vacuoles met within a second, and, allowed to fuse, ten merged into one to five. Meeting is not what limits growth; material is. At the rate measured after splenectomy, all the vacuoles an average cell makes in its 120-day life fuse into one body 0.6 $\mu$m across, the size healthy cells carry, but 16 times smaller in volume than the 1.5-$\mu$m bodies of patients without a spleen. Taking vacuole size as set at formation, a population model in which vacuoles are made mainly in young cells, and far faster in a small minority that alone makes material for a large one, accounts for the published counts, sizes and age profiles and, on first-hand measurements, favours a splenic clearance that rises several-fold as cells age; letting that minority's vacuoles fuse fits nearly as well. At a model splenic slit, the cell's spare surface decided passage, and a vacuole mattered only when it led. A slit experiment would test whether brief encounters fuse vacuoles.
item.dc:creator: Zhaojie Chai, Jianlu Zheng, He Li, Ming Dao, George Em Karniadakis
